about: The content ledger: every content family and what must hold for it. A session picks one entry, works on it, and leaves the evidence. `checks` name gates: shots:NAME (a golden in crates/backrooms/tests/golden/), style:PURPOSE (a band in docs/design/STYLE.md), test:CRATE/FILE (an integration test file), lint:placer-smoke (the placer crates' smoke tests). `passes` and `last_human_review` are written by the drift sweep (cargo xtask drift) and by people; tests/structure.rs keeps the ledger in step with the code.

entries.name: the Showroom
entries.notes: Known look issue: the department signs read as dark plates (tests/materials.rs EXEMPT).

entries.name: the self-assembly: the siren, the fog, the cells, and what knocks at your cell
entries.notes: Half as long since the second pass (G2: a 21 s siren, the fog up 20-40 s, quiets of 38-55 s; a cell within 8 tiles of every floor, held by tests/assembly.rs; tests/pacing.rs the_building_paces_its_floors meets a siren on 11 of 12 floors, no death). What knocks at a sealed cell (G6) goes if left unanswered, tries the wheel if knocked back, and the door gives unless the wheel is held (tests/assembly.rs: silent, answered, held, let go, unsealed; tests/listen.rs the_wheel_is_tried_and_the_door_gives). Since docs/plan/MILESTONES.md 13 its prompts follow what is heard and seen at the door: the hold shows from the wheel's first pull, which takes up the wheel's play first so a press a reaction after it holds the wheel unturned (the_hold_shows_when_the_wheel_turns, held_is_safe), and however it goes it is heard going (its hold slipping from the wheel, then something wet drawn off the door and away, four breaths: not steps, nothing walks the Building), the door to open coming back once it has gone (tests/listen.rs what_knocks_is_heard_going, beside the cell's own lamp, above 1.2 kHz). Whether the siren reads as a warning the first time, whether waiting in a cell is dread or a chore, whether players answer, find the hold and find a door that gives fair, are playtest questions. The siren, the wheel, the door giving and the going are synthesized; no person has listened to them. Knocking, it goes only once its last knock has rung out (its knock to be answered until then); answered, it knocks no more; and its knocking carries above the cell's lamp's hum (a knuckle's click and the leaf's ring, as the residents' knock since 12). Since code review 4b each of its pulls against your hold is heard over that hum too (the spokes slipping and gripping, a creak of steel at 1.9 and 2.9 kHz; what_knocks_is_heard_going, which fails with it at gain 0); no person has listened to it.

entries.name: the Building's floors: heights, walks, flights, voids, cells (in booths over the void where no building is near), the rooms off the walks, a dead end that always holds something, the door seen from the arrival
entries.notes: Navigation measured, not judged: whether finding the way down is a puzzle or a chore is a playtest question. Half as long since the second pass (G1: 28 tiles a side, the way a median 83-87 tiles, every band of tests/building.rs held). tests/building_floors.rs holds the way and what is off it on 72 floors (G3: every dead end holds something) and the rooms off the walks (G4: reached, closed, off the way, holding water or a battery; preferred blind 5 of 5 to the bare walls). The small faults of docs/plan/MILESTONES.md 11 mended (the Works' pipes as runs, the Stair Halls' lanterns, no two lamps in one place, soffits under the flights, the rooms' ceiling, bench and furniture, a post over the panel joint in a Well room's back corners, a room darker than its walk), preferred blind 20 to 0 with 1 tie; tests/building_floors.rs keeps the lamps apart and the rooms darker than their walks. The visual playtest (docs/research/playtests/visual/2026-11-13-building-1-3.md; tests/visual_tour.rs) toured every edge a body reaches on levels 1-3 of two runs: the cell doors' frames no longer fight their piers (F1), the Works' rail posts neither fight their rails nor leave them floating (F6, review B); open, the lamp posts a body walks through (F7, docs/plan/MILESTONES.md 15).

entries.name: the Building's photographed surfaces: the panel facade and its lit windows, whitewash, formwork, yard and factory concrete, rock-faced and floor granite, ribbed slabs
entries.notes: CC0 photographs of Soviet-era places (assets/src/textures/sources.json), built by cargo xtask assets textures; judged blind against the canvas surfaces with cargo xtask ab (tests/review/verdicts.jsonl). No person has looked yet. The visual playtest (docs/research/playtests/visual/2026-11-13-building-1-3.md) left open the metalwork's flat paint among the photographs (F4, docs/plan/MILESTONES.md 16: the props' settled look on it was not preferred blind) and the photographs magnified at inside corners (F5, 17).

entries.name: the Building's torn notes (the residents' notice, a cell plate, the cleaners' log, three surveys, a coupon) and her camp in a cell
entries.notes: They lie only on levels 1-3, two a floor, and no other notes lie there. The residents' notice also says to answer no knock until it is over, to hold the wheel if it turns, and not to knock where the cleaners have marked (G5, G6); the cleaners' log and the Well's survey tell of a knock answered (G5). Reviewed by the lore-keeper (B6, B8, G5, G8); whether the residents' voice reads as the Building's and not hers is a playtest question.

entries.name: what is seen across the Building's void: a person in a long grey work coat who turns away, the Well's lift cage, the door's light from the arrival, the Works' last door
entries.notes: The figure is small on screen by design (22-60 m off); whether it is noticed at all, and whether noticing it is dread, are playtest questions. Its visibility is judged by rules (solids, the dressing over the walks, a backdrop), not by the renderer. Since G7 a person (MakeHuman, CC0; tests/presences.rs the_figure_is_a_person_standing_on_its_perch), preferred blind to the old figure on 15 of 15 images; it stands on a level landing on the Stair Halls' flights and is chosen in the Well only where its parapet hides no more than its legs (docs/plan/MILESTONES.md 2).

entries.name: a knock at the Well's sealed doors: four ordinary doors a floor answer once (water, a battery, a resident's word of the way), a red door knocks back and calls the siren, a taped door never answers, nobody answers while it is up
entries.notes: Its rules are held by tests/knock.rs and its sounds by tests/listen.rs, away from the lamps and beside them (within a few metres of a cell's lamp its hum is the bed, and since docs/plan/MILESTONES.md 12 your raps, someone at the door, the thing pushed out and the knock back carry above it); whether players knock at all, read the red crosses and the tape before they learn them, and whether the answer feels like a reward or a trap, are playtest questions. The answer and the knock back are synthesized; no person has listened to them.

entries.name: Hound
entries.notes: Rebuilt on the new brain and body (docs/design/ENTITIES.md, E2): blind, it hunts by sound along the way it would walk; its counter is held to its arena (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Its body is MakeHuman's CC0 old man posed on all fours (assets/src/creatures/body_hound.py). Beatable with it about (E8): the rule-follower finishes every level of tests/beatable.rs, no death breaking a fairness rule, and the whole run is played live; what it learns is held to its arena too (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Whether it frightens is for people (docs/research/PLAYTEST.md, The creatures). Judged blind against the old Hound (E10): preferred at 2 and 4 m and at its death, not at 8 m (pale against the wall). Its motion is Kimodo's clips (E11): a person crawling on hands and knees, the knees standing for its feet, hands and feet planted, quickened into its lope and its scrabbling charge, the left hind dragging; judged blind against its procedural animation, preferred on its lope and its charge, ties on its search and spring. Heavy and upright since E12 (standing part of the way out of its stoop, its weight sinking onto each footfall, uncanny and never a cartoon), judged blind against E11's motion. Remade in E13 from researched references within its canon (docs/research/hound-references.md): its body (bent knees, the hump, the hanging head, clawed hands, bone under the skin, worn and torn cloth, matted hair) and its motion (prowling, a dead stop at a sound, its head turned to it). Monsters, not dolls (E14, docs/research/creature-horror-references.md): it still read as a doll, smooth, pale and glossy, its face a bald egg; now dry, mottled, filthy skin (with_skin: no sheen, its creases dark), kneecaps, the shin's edge, elbows, tendons and knuckles, sores where it kneels, loose skin at its joints, long cracked nails, its face's lids grown shut and its mouth a slack gape, near-black hair plastered over the crown and combed forward to hang over the face; 101k triangles near, a far body of 22.7k from 6 m (tests/bodies.rs). Preferred blind to E13's by two fresh reviewers, 7 of 7 frames each (with the Smiler's), both orders.

entries.name: Smiler
entries.notes: Rebuilt on the new brain and body (docs/design/ENTITIES.md, E3): it sees your lamp from far off and your lit body only near; lamp off and still, it loses you; running near it makes it lunge; slow in bright rooms. Its counter is held to its arena (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Its body is MakeHuman's CC0 young thin man, stretched and wasted, its face sculpted to the skull and its teeth built one by one (assets/src/creatures/body_smiler.py). Beatable with it about (E8): the rule-follower finishes every level of tests/beatable.rs, no death breaking a fairness rule, and the whole run is played live; what it learns is held to its arena too (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Whether it frightens is for people (docs/research/PLAYTEST.md, The creatures). Its body redone after a blind review read it as a black body suit (E10: deeper ribs, dust dried on the bones, a wider, paler grin; its skin left dull, since wet read as latex): preferred to its first body at 2 m by two reviewers, ties elsewhere, and to the old Smiler at 2, 4 and 8 m and at its death. Its motion is Kimodo's clips (E11): a person creeping, stalking, sprinting and lunging, laid on its stoop, with its wrongness on top (held frames and snaps searching, the head first, dead arms); judged blind against its procedural animation, preferred on its search, stalk, run, lunge and withdrawal. Heavy and upright since E12 (standing part of the way out of its stoop, its weight sinking onto each footfall, uncanny and never a cartoon), judged blind against E11's motion. Monsters, not dolls (E14, docs/research/creature-horror-references.md): its wet black read as latex, its teeth as a denture; now a dry near-black crust cracked into plates (pale dust in the cracks, red-brown under them), the neck's cords, collarbones, breastbone, hip bones, kneecaps and tendons standing out, long black nails, teeth stained ivory to brown, uneven, gapped and broken, one side of its lips higher, one shoulder lower; 61k triangles near, a far body of 19k from 6 m (tests/bodies.rs). Preferred blind to the old by two fresh reviewers, 7 of 7 frames each (with the Hound's), both orders.

entries.name: the one in the corner
entries.notes: New in the redesign (docs/design/ENTITIES.md, E5): placed in a quiet corner off the way, never sent; harmless while you see its back; its face seen (or come round into your eyes as it looks round, the hum stopped first) wakes it: it screams and comes. Its counter is held to its arena (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Its body is MakeHuman's CC0 old thin tall man, its eyes and mouth flipped upside down, in a nightshirt draped by Blender's cloth (assets/src/creatures/body_corner.py). Beatable with it about (E8): the rule-follower finishes every level of tests/beatable.rs, no death breaking a fairness rule, and the whole run is played live; what it learns is held to its arena too (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Whether it frightens is for people (docs/research/PLAYTEST.md, The creatures). Its motion is Kimodo's clips (E11): it holds with none of a person's sway, runs a sprinter's run with dead arms, walks back stiffly; judged blind, preferred on its run; the old animation preferred on the walk back to its corner (small stiff steps under the nightshirt read as standing still). Heavy and upright since E12 (standing part of the way out of its stoop, its weight sinking onto each footfall, uncanny and never a cartoon), judged blind against E11's motion.

entries.name: the one behind the glass
entries.notes: New with the windows (docs/design/WINDOWS.md 4): placed behind one window of about four in ten floors with windows, never sent; your eyes on its glass add up: it ticks, comes up the track only while you look, comes to the glass on its own in its lamp's light and through it, and inside is held to the lamp's light on the floor; a blind let down (or paper over the glass) keeps it out and puts its light out; got away from twice, its lamp hangs lower. Its rules one test a line on real floors (tests/glass.rs: no arena, a window needs a real wall). Its body is MakeHuman's CC0 young thin man and woman, half each, in a raincoat, its skirt draped by Blender's cloth and its hood a shell of its own (assets/src/creatures/body_glass.py). Whether it frightens is for people (docs/research/PLAYTEST.md, The creatures). Its motion is Kimodo's clips (E11): a walk too even (no rise and fall, arms still), a crouch through the window, a walk with its arms out inside, backing out facing you; judged blind, preferred on its walk, its reach and its backing out, a tie through the window. Heavy and upright since E12 (standing part of the way out of its stoop, its weight sinking onto each footfall, uncanny and never a cartoon), judged blind against E11's motion.

entries.name: the Reader
entries.notes: New in the redesign (docs/design/ENTITIES.md, E6): a thin man bent over a sheet held before its face, whispering what it reads; it sees you over the page within 12 m, and only lit or moving, and comes faster than you walk. Its counter is paper: any sheet on the floor within 4 m of it, it must pick up and read to the end (the sheets you drop, and the piles lying about, once each); it never touches her folded sheets nor the flat ones (tests/story.rs). Placed beside paper lying about, from depth 2, and sent like the Smiler and the Hound. Its counter is held to its arena (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Its body is MakeHuman's CC0 thin man, its fingers half as long again, in a cardigan, trousers and shoes grown off the skin (assets/src/creatures/body_reader.py). Beatable with it about (E8): the rule-follower finishes every level of tests/beatable.rs, no death breaking a fairness rule, and the whole run is played live; what it learns is held to its arena too (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Whether it frightens is for people (docs/research/PLAYTEST.md, The creatures). Its motion is Kimodo's clips (E11): a person walking reading a page, stooping for a sheet, hurrying, tearing it; its page work on top (the eyes along the lines, the look up); judged blind, preferred on its reading walk, its hurry, its stoop (second round, after the page was brought back to its face) and its walking away. Heavy and upright since E12 (standing part of the way out of its stoop, its weight sinking onto each footfall, uncanny and never a cartoon), judged blind against E11's motion.

entries.name: the Watcher
entries.notes: Rebuilt on the new brain and body (docs/design/ENTITIES.md, E4): it moves only unseen and only when sent; its touch knocks you down and takes your nerve, killing only a spent mind; silent, your ears ring near it. Its counter is held to its arena (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Its body is one dust sheet draped by Blender's cloth over MakeHuman's CC0 old man, its six poses the same sheet draped again (assets/src/creatures/body_watcher.py); it stands among furniture under the same sheets (sheeted.py). Beatable with it about (E8): the rule-follower finishes every level of tests/beatable.rs, no death breaking a fairness rule, and the whole run is played live; what it learns is held to its arena too (tests/creatures_arenas.rs). Whether it frightens is for people (docs/research/PLAYTEST.md, The creatures). Its body redone after a blind review read it as a bedsheet ghost (E10: a narrow shroud over a 1.96 m man, where his eyes and open mouth are the cloth grimed dark, each pose's face on the same part of the sheet): preferred to its first body at every distance and its death by two reviewers; the old Watcher (a tall robe with a face showing through) is still preferred at 2 and 4 m and at its death.

entries.name: bathroom props (29 placers)
entries.notes: P1-P3: the washroom's things remade as real ones (the mirrors, the basin and the rest), their draws kept; P4 wear; M8: a silvered mirror shows the lamp as a small hot spot, the nail polish's drip a flat run, the atomizer (a tie).

entries.name: core props (70 placers)
entries.notes: P1-P3 (docs/design/PROPS.md): every cartoon kind of the core props remade as the real thing in Blender batches r01-r18 at its real size, its print painted, its draws kept call for call (the reference levels hold every placer's objects); P4: wear by use, the thing's own (tests/prop_wear.rs); M8: contact shadows under small things on the floor, a mirror's lamp a hot spot; P5 the barricades and P6 the verbs have entries of their own. P7: the place's own flames (the candles on the bench, a haunted floor's candles) only where the verbs are, below the Lobby and never on a floor with rules of its own; a candle blown out stays out; the bench says nothing, its hum comes from it and by it the low-nerve heartbeat holds off (tests/flames.rs, tests/player.rs; LORE.md What still burns). The light switch's '(bad wiring)', the vacuum's and the payphone's dice and lines, the shaft's lines and the staff ID's names still break the house style (docs/research/props-interactions.md 1.3). No person has judged a prop.

entries.name: domestic props (96 placers)
entries.notes: P1-P3: someone's rooms' things remade as real ones (the kettle, the books, the rugs, the shoes and the rest), their draws kept; P4 wear; M8 (the suitcase's jumpers, the umbrella crooks). What burns is canon (LORE.md What still burns, P7): the cigarette left burning in a glass ashtray, a kettle's vapour and an iron's steam.

entries.name: industrial props (32 placers)
entries.notes: P1-P3: the maintenance runs' things remade as real ones (the rusted pipes and their leak, the breaker panel, the firewood and the rest), their draws kept; P4 wear. The wall placers take a pool's curb for a wall (open).

entries.name: nature props (16 placers)
entries.notes: P2-P3: the overgrown atrium's things remade as real ones (the dead geraniums and the rest), their draws kept; P4 wear; M8 (the conker husks, a tie: whether they read as petals is for people).

entries.name: occult props (15 placers)
entries.notes: P3: the shrine's things remade as real ones (t08, t09, t17, t18 and others: the candlestick, the memorial board, the pumpkins and cauldrons, the censer), their draws kept; P4 wear; M8's shape fixes (the mask's ribbons). What burns is canon (LORE.md What still burns, P7): the candles lit or cold as the code draws them, the censer cold, no coal and no smoke. Whether a lit candle in an empty shrine reads as wrong or as a game's light is for people.

entries.name: office props (76 placers)
entries.notes: P1-P3: the office's things remade as real ones (the wall phone, the chalkboard and the rest), their draws kept; P4 wear. P7: a mug's coffee still steams and a broken wall phone's board still smokes (LORE.md What still burns).

entries.name: party props (21 placers)
entries.notes: P3: the party's paper, the cake stand and its cake nobody ate (t13) and the rest, their draws kept; P4 wear. What burns is canon (LORE.md What still burns, P7): a birthday candle lit or out as the code draws it.

entries.name: toys props (43 placers)
entries.notes: P1-P3: the toys remade as real, faded ones (the baby doll, the duck, the ball, the plush and the rest), their draws kept; P4 wear; M8: contact shadows under the small things on the floor (9 of 9), the doll's limbs apart, the elephant's ears.

entries.name: victorian props (43 placers)
entries.notes: P3: the parlour's things remade as real ones (t10 the fireplace and the wall bookshelf, t21 the hanging brass lantern, and others), their draws kept; P4 wear; M8 (the bookshelf's brackets, the roe head, the trout). What burns is canon (LORE.md What still burns, P7): the hanging lantern and the chandelier always lit, about half the hearths and sconces cold, a lit hearth's crackle heard close by, the tray's tea still steaming.

entries.name: voice lines: personas, their lines, the evaluation, and your asides' voice director (docs/design/VOICES.md)
entries.notes: made and judged outside the check (cargo xtask voice build | eval | selftest, which need the Python environments and the models); the check holds the shipped files to the manifest and the index (structure, xtask voice tests, game audio::voice tests) and hears the cry (listen: the_cry_is_your_voice). A person has not listened yet. Your asides (you_aside, 90 lines over sixteen uses; issue #10 added met, odd, noticed and used, and notes and beds to found): made, judged and reviewed by lore-keeper outside the check; the check holds the director's rules (game audio::asides tests), the hooks and the whole game (backrooms/asides), the pacing (backrooms/pacing: nothing chosen in a peak; eight runs differ), and hears an arrival (listen: an_arrival_is_your_voice_under_your_breath). A person has not listened to one yet. Your voice on the way in (you_tunnel, 26 lines, use way_in; the tunnel's, docs/design/WAY_IN.md): made and judged outside the check (every line has a take that passes), reviewed by lore-keeper; the check holds its order and reactions (game modes::tunnel_voice tests, backrooms/tunnel), its canon (game audio::voice no_line_on_the_way_in_names_what_the_canon_keeps_unsaid) and hears it over the tunnel (listen: the_way_in_is_your_voice_over_the_hum_and_the_cars). A person has not listened yet.

entries.name: M.'s trail (her marks)

Whether people read the small marks as hers, and find them in the dark, is untested with people.

entries.notes: Two to four places a floor off the way (one at most on the Lobby), each kind with its tell; the run lays its thirteen things over the first descent; the hole gives back and takes; the notebook's page keeps what and where. Whether people find them by the tell or the sign, and whether they start lifting every tile, is untested with people.

entries.name: the things a hand can use (docs/design/PROPS.md 3, LORE.md Within reach: a box, a bin, a book stack, a locker left unlocked, a dead lift, the television)
entries.notes: none on the Building's floors, the Lobby or a floor with rules of its own; what each holds is fixed when the floor is built, from a stream of its own (USE_SALT), given once (what_they_give_is_fixed_and_given_once); each verb where its prop is (every_usable_prop_has_its_verb); the TV off and on (the_tv_switches_off_and_on); the tape, a locker and a set coming on stop a creature near, a bin and a page do not (a_loud_verb_stops_what_is_near_and_a_quiet_one_does_not); the sounds are synthesized, no person has listened to them or used a verb What is picked up is gone (issue #12; what_is_picked_up_is_gone: every bottle, battery, stack of paper and note of levels 1-12 on four seeds, and what the drawers give, stood on, taken, given once, not drawn again nor its shadow); the props' cull hides by a flag of its own (the_cull_hides_what_is_far_and_never_shows_what_was_hidden).

entries.name: what still burns (docs/design/LORE.md: the candles, lanterns and fires people left, the candles on the bench, a haunted floor's candles; the cold censer)
entries.notes: Canon from the code's gates and draws (P7): the themed ones only where their purpose welcomes them, lit or cold by their own draws, never burning down; the place's own (the bench, a haunted floor's candles) where the verbs are, below the Lobby and never on a floor with rules of its own (the_place_burns_nothing_on_the_lobby_or_a_floor_of_its_own); a candle blown out stays out (a_candle_blown_out_stays_out); the bench mends the nerve 3.2x, holds off the heartbeat and says nothing (dark_regions_drain_and_safe_rooms_mend). No person has stood at the bench or blown out a candle.

entries.name: the writing on the walls (docs/design/PROPS.md 4, LORE.md Writing on the walls: what people trapped here wrote, in what an office has, baked into the wall)
entries.notes: issue #11: seven media an office could give (dried blood, correction fluid, marker, lipstick, a scratch, ballpoint, pencil), a hand that wavers, crowds, fades and crosses out, 25 lines dealt by the run, none twice on a floor and none on the Lobby, in the Showroom or the Borrowed House; baked into the face of the wall behind it, under its light (writing_is_baked_into_its_wall: thin, on a drawn face, world UVs off, never over a window); the old choice's draws kept (core_props_tail, reference_levels: only the writing moves); game core_props::graffiti unit tests hold the media, sizes, fading, the deal and the glyphs. A blind A/B review of four cameras before and after (2026-11-15). No person has read one on a wall yet.

entries.name: the assets made by the pipeline (docs/design/ASSETS.md: a dossier each in assets/src/props/, placement rules the game reads): almond water, the battery (also the Loop's, and the yellowish one put away); the doors (docs/plan/DOORS.md): the exit door and its sign (also the Loop's side doors), the steel door (also the Stairwell's top and bottom doors), the hermetic door (the cells and the Well's galleries), the lift doors (the working, the dead and the broken lift), the interior door (the door to nowhere, the barricade's door); the lamps (docs/plan/FACILITY.md F3): the high-bay (the tall halls), the bulkhead (the tunnels' crown); the Utility Halls' runs (docs/plan/FACILITY.md F5): the service run (a tray of cables, a pair of pipes on hangers)
entries.notes: issue #13: each made from its brief (what it is, how it came here, what a hand does), references of both licences (free ones by checksum, limited ones only looked at), a Blender model at its real size and its own materials, and placement rules each with its why; the game places the floor's own by them (what_the_rules_place_keeps_its_rules: purpose, surface or a wall's foot, the dark where a rule says, apart, counts), they are picked up and gone (what_is_picked_up_is_gone), the parts lint holds the meshes; cargo xtask asset check holds the dossiers (xtask tests). The playtest's "why could this be here?" asked twice of a fresh placement-critic each (their playtest.md); a blind review against the old. No person has asked it yet. Reviewed (A7, a fresh lore-keeper and code-reviewer): every bottle sealed (the yellowish one put away, built by the same builder, the only one opened), the cell HALDEN's; a thing on a surface rests on the stand's own top (rays in the test), one pass for any asset marked by rules, the Loop's pickups the same parts (loop_rooms), the bundle held to its sources. The doors (D1, 2026-11-16): the exit door (a flush red-oak veneered office door, 914 x 2134 x 44 mm, its pressed-steel frame, lever, closer and kick plate, the lit exit sign 400 x 200 mm with no arrow, the Works' warm under it) and the steel door (the Stairwell's way in, its STAIRS plaque), from their dossiers (references of both licences, read by a lore-keeper); made by the layout, held to their rules (what_the_layout_places_keeps_its_rules: one way down on every floor of 48). D2-D5: the Stairwell's two doors and the Loop's (its way in, its side doors), the hermetic door (every cell and the Well's galleries, the door that knocks), the lift doors (the working, the dead and the broken lift; the shaft's look moved with them), the interior door (the door to nowhere, the barricade's). D6 (2026-11-17): why could this be here? asked of each (a fresh placement-critic, 44 frames; each playtest.md): the back of the house's way down is the steel door, the lifts set nearly flush; a wall-width check taken out (MILESTONES.md 26). Blind review: the new door preferred at 9 of 10 cameras, both orders; the working lift lost four rounds (MILESTONES.md 27). The visual playtest of six door areas (docs/research/playtests/visual/2026-11-17-doors.md), its flicker fixed. A fresh code review's findings fixed: made against recorded in the layout test, the_doors_are_built_of_their_parts, the Stairwell's regen guarded. The bench: the same as before the doors, interleaved (a VM's load set a first run over budget). The lamps (F3, 2026-11-17): the high-bay and the jar lamp from their dossiers (20 references), made by the layout ("lamp") and held to their rules; their playtest asked once (the high-bay only under a tall bare slab); blind, the new lamps preferred at 5 of 9 cameras over two rounds (the tubes where a hall is seen from an office).

entries.name: the Utility Halls as a plant's service tunnels (docs/plan/FACILITY.md F5): sprayed concrete walls and crown, haunches with a row of bolts, the runs on the straight corridors' crown
entries.notes: world::lining; the sprayed concrete a CC0 photograph (ambientCG Concrete037, assets/src/textures/build.py shotcrete and shotcrete_grain), the generator's table keeping the old game's concrete (world::lining::wall_mat_of); the runs a dossier (assets/src/props/service_run/). Judged blind twice against the formwork boxes they replaced (tests/review/verdicts.jsonl: 7 of 7 each time); the placement playtest 4 of 4 obvious; the visual playtest docs/research/playtests/visual/2026-11-17-utility-halls.md. No person has looked yet; the jar lamp's canopy left one paint among worn runs is a question for one.

entries.name: the Habitable Zone as a column hall (docs/plan/FACILITY.md F6): walls and columns painted two-tone, a bare slab cast against steel forms, columns flared into drop panels, no windows
entries.notes: world::halls and world::lining::wall_mat_of / ceil_mat_of; the paint a CC0 photograph (Poly Haven painted_plaster_wall, assets/src/textures/build.py twotone), its band 0.8 m high so her pencil's marks stay on the pale; the slab the Works' formwork photograph. Judged blind twice against the bare formwork halls (tests/review/verdicts.jsonl: 7 of 7, then 6 of 7, the one a close view of a sheet of standing water, since dropped). The visual playtest docs/research/playtests/visual/2026-11-17-habitable-zone.md. No person has looked yet.

entries.name: railed drops cut into the Habitable Zone's halls (docs/plan/FACILITY.md F7): pits of a floor, standing water or the dark, the Works' railing round them, catwalks of bar grating over the lit ones
entries.notes: world::drops; a pit's tiles are walls of the grid whose solid is a void (it stops a body), a catwalk's are floor (creatures cross it too); the walls built as before the cut; nothing put on a drop or hung at its edge (Game::is_hang_wall, Game::is_drop_tile). level_sweep holds it: drops_stop_a_body_and_their_catwalks_are_walked, nothing_is_put_on_a_drop_or_hung_on_its_edge, a_drop_changes_no_wall_but_its_own. Judged blind twice against the halls before (tests/review/verdicts.jsonl: 3 to 2 with a tie, the columns at a drop's edge broken; then 6 of 6 with them kept). The lore-keeper read the canon twice. The visual playtest docs/research/playtests/visual/2026-11-18-drops.md. No person has looked yet.

entries.name: the vault (docs/plan/FACILITY.md F8): a new archetype, one long arched chamber, bare concrete or corrugated liner plate, its lamps on cords and its cobwebs leaning toward a blind end
entries.notes: level::archgen::vault (FACILITY_ARCHETYPES beside the old game's table: archgen_tables untouched; picked by a zone's shape on the facility's floors from depth 6; its ends hard against the repair tunnels) and world::vaults (the arch, its webs, the draught settled away from doors). The liner plate a CC0 photograph (Poly Haven corrugated_iron_02, assets/src/textures/build.py liner). level_sweep holds it: nothing_pokes_through_a_vaults_arch, a_vaults_draught_leans_toward_a_closed_end. Judged blind against the floors before (tests/review/verdicts.jsonl: 6 of 6, both orders). The lore-keeper read the canon; the developer chose the wrong thing and the caption THE VAULTS. No person has looked yet.

entries.name: the pit hall (docs/plan/FACILITY.md F9): a new archetype, a hall of open concrete tanks of murky water in rows, the floor between them, railed, catwalks across some, columns rising out of the water; every tank wet a hand or more above its water
entries.notes: level::archgen::pits (beside the vault in FACILITY_ARCHETYPES; the largest hall at least 9 tiles across on a facility floor with no anomaly, by its shape; carved open, its tanks from pit_tanks) and world::pits (each tank a drop of world::drops with its water, its wet band and its columns; its high-bays over its walkways; never dark nor papered; no pool; nothing of water going somewhere left there, Game::clear_pits_of_water; no drip anchored or sounding there). level_sweep holds it: a_pit_halls_tanks_are_wet_above_their_water, and the drops' own tests over its tanks (to level 16). Judged blind against the floors before (tests/review/verdicts.jsonl: 8 of 8, both orders). The lore-keeper read the canon; the developer chose its shape, its columns, its wrong thing and the caption THE PIT HALLS. No person has looked yet.

entries.name: the cutscene engine: storage, the player, the bars, the test engine

entries.name: New descent: from the title's view into your eyes
entries.notes: Three Wells (4242, 7, 9001). Seamless when the title shows a run nobody has played; through black over another run's floor.

entries.name: the way in: the look into the tunnel
entries.notes: From the street above the stairs, down both flights, across the plaza, under the arch and into your eyes a few bays in the walkway. Begins 0.3 s after the place is up behind the black, from the camera as it is. Two stages (tunnel:4242, tunnel:7).

entries.name: a broken lift's shaft: the black, a breath, what looks back
entries.notes: Three lifts (three facings). The lift itself stands on the Lobby with blood and remains (QUALITY.md, Canon).

entries.name: a creature's kill: its face, the fall, black
entries.notes: Every creature's kill; the card at 1.4 s; shorter on a repeat; the draws after it as before.

entries.name: your nerve gives out: your knees, the floor, black
entries.notes: No golden yet.

entries.name: the fog takes you: sinking into the violet, black
entries.notes: No golden yet.
